title: Democrats to hold a dozen 2028 presidential primary debates starting in June
summary:
DNC unveils plans to hold 12 primary debates over 10 months, allowing up to 20 candidates to participate

The Democratic National Committee (DNC)

blocks.text: The Democratic National Committee (DNC) unveiled on Monday its plans to hold a dozen 2028 presidential primary debates over 10 months, with the first set to take place in June.

Between June 2027 and March 2028, the DNC will host 12 debates, allowing up to 20 candidates to participate, so long as they agree to new criteria. That includes pledging to reject “dark money” – or funding from outside groups that do not disclose their donors – and not participating in unsanctioned debates.
The announcement came just weeks after Democrats swept the midterm elections and won majorities in the House, Senate and governor’s offices.

“Democrats are on offense after our historic victories in the midterms, and the DNC is keeping our foot on the gas as we head into the 2028 cycle,” Ken Martin, the DNC chair, said in a statement. “The fair and transparent process and experienced leadership team we’re announcing today will keep our party united, strengthen our eventual nominee, and put Democrats in position to take back the White House.”
Though no candidates have officially announced their 2028 presidential bid, the Democratic field is expected to be large.

Several names have been floated as potential contenders, including Gavin Newsom, the governor of California; Kamala Harris, the former vice-president and 2024 Democratic presidential nominee; Josh Shapiro, the governor of Pennsylvania; JB Pritzker, the governor of Illinois; Andy Beshear, the governor of Kentucky, and more.

But early polling among Democratic primary voters shows that party members would more likely support a younger and more progressive candidate. In an Emerson College Poll, 17% of respondents said they would support Jon Ossoff, the Georgia senator, while 12% said they would support the New York congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.
In a Reuters/Ipsos poll, 29% of respondents believed Pete Buttigieg, the former secretary of transportation, and Ossoff would make excellent presidential candidates.

Ocasio-Cortez has not announced any plans to run for president, but progressive organizers are hopeful she’ll throw her hat into the ring. Recently, hundreds of organizers from Ready for AOC, a new group, held a Zoom call to try to convince Ocasio-Cortez to launch a presidential campaign.

Buttigieg similarly has not announced a campaign, but allies of the former transportation secretary are launching a grassroots effort to try to inspire him to make a second bid for president, Politico reported.
Given how large the primary field may be, the DNC said early debates may be held over two consecutive nights, in which qualifying candidates will randomly be assigned a night to participate.

Like in past primaries, candidates who qualify for the primary will need to meet certain polling criteria among other qualifications. The DNC said it would announce its specific criteria for the first two debates in January, but that it will include measures to reflect a candidate’s support, such as grassroots funding.
Among other new features, the DNC’s debates will incorporate “creators and influencers” in the process, though they did not elaborate on what their role may be.
The DNC will release more information in January about the dates, locations and media partners of the first two debates.
